projects.title: MotoGP 25
projects.subtitle: Milestone S.r.l. — AAA Motorcycle Racing
projects.description: During my second project at Milestone, I was responsible for testing the game's content, whilst also creating new test cases for the team to use, as well as conducting performance and analytics tests. I also developed my skills as a Tech QA Analyst; this project, too, resulted in a submission that passed with flying colours and a successful international launch.
projects.longDescription: RIDE 6 is the latest chapter in Milestone's acclaimed motorcycle racing franchise. As a QA Tester and Tech QA Analyst, my work covered functional testing of game content, performance profiling across platforms, and creating structured test cases used by the full QA team. Working at this scale — across PC, PS5, and Xbox — sharpened my ability to identify platform-specific issues, communicate clearly with developers, and meet certification deadlines under pressure.

projects.title: Narciso's Dream
projects.subtitle: Event Horizon School — GameLab 1
projects.description: In this first completely free-themed GameLab, we tried to develop a Top-Down Arena featuring dynamic combat and a dreamlike setting, with the assets changing from a dream version to a nightmare version as the game progresses and the player takes damage. Will you manage not to get trapped in the nightmare?
projects.longDescription: Narciso's Dream was the first GameLab project at Event Horizon School — a two-week sprint with no fixed theme, giving our 17-person team full creative freedom. I took on the dual role of Game Designer and Project Manager, defining the core loop of a Top-Down Arena where the visual aesthetic shifts dynamically between a dreamy, peaceful state and a dark nightmare as the player takes damage. Managing a team of this size under tight deadlines taught me how to balance creative ambition with pragmatic scoping.

projects.title: Dwarf Keeper
projects.subtitle: Event Horizon School — GameLab 2
projects.description: My first project at Milestone as a QA Tester. I contributed to functional testing and quality assurance, helping the title reach certification successfully.
projects.longDescription: Working on my first professional title at Milestone S.r.l. was a pivotal experience. I joined the QA team for this project and was responsible for executing test plans, logging and tracking bugs through the pipeline, and verifying fixes. The project completed certification and launched internationally, marking my entry into the professional games industry.

projects.title: Hover Remake
projects.subtitle: Event Horizon School — Remakes
projects.description: This remake of Hover was the first team project done at Event Horizon School during January 2024. The remake is a faithful reproduction of the famous 1995 game, in a revamped graphic design. Capture all the blue flags before the enemies manage to capture the red ones!
projects.longDescription: The Hover Remake was my team's first project at Event Horizon School — a faithful reimagining of the classic 1995 Windows game, rebuilt in Unity with a fresh visual identity. Over three weeks with an 18-member team, I coordinated game design decisions and production flow, ensuring we preserved what made the original charming while modernising the look and feel. This project laid the foundation for how I approach team leadership in game development.

projects.title: Seedious Sam XD: The Last Farmer
projects.subtitle: Global Game Jam 2023 — Milan
projects.description: Developed during the Global Game Jam 2023, from the theme "Roots", in this chaotic local 1v1 party game two players will compete over a land overrun by roots using genetically modified plants as weapons. Which of the two will prevail?
projects.longDescription: 48 hours, 7 people, one theme: "Roots". Seedious Sam XD: The Last Farmer is the chaotic local 1v1 party game that came out of Global Game Jam 2023 in Milan. As Game Designer and Team Lead, I pitched the concept, delegated tasks, and kept the team focused through an intense weekend of development. The result: a frenetic plant-based battle game where two players weaponise genetically modified crops in a last-farmer-standing showdown.

projects.title: Totally Inaccurate Solar System Simulator
projects.subtitle: Coursera — Michigan State University
projects.description: In this platformer, created solo during my first approach to development on Unity, you take on the role of an explorer who must enter the realm of Ekrund, an ancient dwarven settlement abandoned after a mysterious event. Traverse the first three levels and immerse yourself in the exploration of the ruins of an ancient civilization.
projects.longDescription: Tales of Ekrund was my first solo Unity project, built as part of Michigan State University's Game Design and Development Specialization on Coursera. Over two weeks, I designed and built a 3-level 2D platformer completely from scratch — handling level design, scripting, and UI. The game follows an explorer delving into Ekrund, a dwarven ruin shrouded in mystery. This project was my real introduction to Unity's workflow and the challenges of solo game development.

projects.title: Athena
projects.subtitle: University of Milan — Online Game Design
projects.description: In this game, created during the Online Game Design course at the Milan University, you can play online with two friends and, choosing different classes, tackle a puzzle platform level together trying to reach Athena, an evil artificial intelligence that has taken control of the university. Will you be able to defeat her by helping each other?
projects.longDescription: Athena was developed during the Online Game Design course at the University of Milan, themed around the institution's centenary. Ten of us built an online co-op puzzle platformer where three players select different ability classes and collaborate to defeat Athena — an AI villain who has seized control of the university. The project was a deep dive into multiplayer architecture in Unity and the design challenges of building mechanics that require genuine cooperation.
